description: A hilly, forested region east of the Jordan settled by the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh, whose territory it shared — which is why Scripture attaches individuals to Gilead without always specifying a single tribe. Jephthah led Gilead's fighting men against Ammon (Judges 10-12), and Elijah was "of the settlers of Gilead" (1 Kings 17:1). It was known for its balm, a valuable healing resin (Genesis 37:25; Jeremiah 8:22).
family_friendly_summary: Gilead was a green, hilly region east of the Jordan River, shared by the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh. The judge Jephthah and the prophet Elijah both came from Gilead. It was famous for a healing ointment called the "balm of Gilead."
